why_this_amendment_exists: Round 1's H1-original FAIL is permanent and is NOT rewritten by this amendment.

H1-original gated 'valid onset/follow-up >= 50 per regime' on the strict reading: an onset counts only if its ENTIRE registered response window is observed inside the task's own observed life. Measured: 24 / 36 / 31 against a threshold of 50, because the median observed cohort life is 5-6 intervals while the registered response horizons are 16-18 intervals. The strict reading is structurally unreachable in this simulator.
The directive therefore registers a second, explicitly named quantity (usable_primary_followup) and a new gate (H1-v2) next to the preserved H1-original verdict.

h1_original.definition: onset whose whole registered response window (horizon = max(window end)) is continuously observed on the task's own timeline
h1_original.permanence: H1-original = FAIL is preserved permanently; it must never be rewritten as PASS, and this amendment does not re-evaluate it

usable_primary_followup.definition: An onset event counts as usable when the task has at least one valid task-level observation inside the first registered downstream resource response window of its own regime.

operationalisation.quantity: count of onset events with >= 1 observation at an interval t with t0 + start <= t < t0 + end, where [start, end) is the regime's registered response window of its first downstream resource
operationalisation.first_downstream_resource_rule: the response resource with the smallest registered window start; this is the next resource in the regime's registered cascade sequence
operationalisation.observation_source: task_timeline rows of the onset task itself (never the host aggregate, never the label)

compute_first.directive_text: A: CPU onset -> RAM window [t0+4, t0+14)

memory_first.directive_text: B: RAM onset -> Disk window [t0+3, t0+13)

io_first.directive_text: C: Disk onset -> CPU window [t0+3, t0+13)

usable_primary_followup.consistency_check: every window above is exactly the 'first downstream' window of the registered cascade_v3 regime (regime files: simulator/workload/BitbrainWorkloadProtocol023.py, REGIMES_V3[*].response_windows); the directive's numbers and the registered numbers agree for all three regimes

reporting_definitions.n_full_window_followup: whole registered response horizon observed (H1-original's own quantity)
reporting_definitions.n_any_window_followup: at least one observation inside ANY registered response window (the Protocol 022 MIN_FOLLOWUP_EVENTS reading; round 1 recorded this as 'usable_followup', not gated)

gate_h1_v2.stop_condition: if ANY regime has primary-window follow-up < 80 -> STOP-DATA-v2 (S4 must not run)

frozen_before_model_runs.calibration_inputs_allowed: data-only statistics computed from stream arrays (label counts, task cohorts, host capacity/aggregate demand); no probe, no learner, no PR-AUC
